Technical Debt & Platform Modernization

Automation & Release Engineering

• Experience designing human-in-the-loop release automation or progressive delivery systems (canary, blue/green)

You will sit with teams across YA Group, learn how their work gets done, find where AI and automation can make it faster, more accurate or less manual, and then build those solutions yourself. This is an internal, hands-on role. You are not selling products or running demos for customers. You will design, build and ship working tools that our people use every day, using modern AI development tools such as Claude Code alongside solid engineering practice. ## In This Role, You Will:
## Understand the business
Spend time with the business to map how work flows today, including the manual steps, handoffs and workarounds. Identify and size opportunities for AI and automation, and help prioritize them by business value and effort. Translate business needs into clear, practical solution designs that non-technical stakeholders can understand and approve.
## Build and ship
Design, build, test and deploy AI-enabled tools, agents, workflow automations and integrations. Use AI-assisted development tools (Claude Code and similar) to move fast, while owning the quality, security and maintainability of what ships. Integrate with our core business systems, including Microsoft 365, Salesforce, NetSuite and Dayforce, through APIs and connectors. Work with our data platform and data owners to get the data your solutions need, in a governed way.
## Architecture and enablement
Contribute to reference architectures and reusable patterns for AI solutions: approved tools, connectors, environments, and how solutions access data. Support builders outside IT, including AI specialists in other departments, with standards, code review and guidance so their work is secure and maintainable. Maintain an inventory of AI solutions across the company: what exists, who owns it and what data it uses.
## Run and improve
Support what you build after launch: monitoring, fixes, documentation and handoff where appropriate. Measure outcomes such as hours saved, error reduction and cycle time, and report them in plain terms. Help triage and manage the queue of AI requests from across the business. Partner with Information Security to put our AI governance framework into practice: tool and vendor evaluation, data access controls, review before production, and lifecycle ownership.

## Required
Hands-on development experience: 3+ years building and shipping software that real users depended on, not only prototypes or personal projects. Strong programming skills in Python and/or TypeScript/JavaScript, with experience in REST APIs, JSON and SQL. Integration experience: connecting business systems through APIs, webhooks or integration platforms. Engineering fundamentals: version control (Git), testing, deployment, logging and error handling. Security awareness: sound handling of credentials, access permissions and sensitive data. Practical AI experience: has built real solutions with large language models (prompting, tool use, retrieval or agents) and uses AI coding tools in daily work, with the judgment to know when to rely on them and when to step in. Solution design: experience designing the architecture of the solutions you build, not only building to someone else's design. AI risk awareness: working knowledge of risks such as data leakage, prompt injection and model limitations, and the governance practices that address them. Business process skills: able to sit with business users, ask good questions, map a workflow and explain technical options in plain language. Ownership: comfortable working independently, managing your own priorities and seeing work through to adoption.

Experience with Microsoft 365 / Microsoft Graph, Salesforce, NetSuite or Dayforce. Experience with the Claude API, Model Context Protocol (MCP) or agent frameworks. Cloud experience (Azure preferred) and familiarity with data warehouses and pipelines. Background in professional services, engineering or another field-based business. Experience working in a SOC 2 or similarly controlled environment.

Build a new capability at a company that is serious about using AI to improve how work gets done. Direct access to leadership and a wide view across the business. Visible impact: your work will be used across the company, not shelved. Remote role with a modern toolset.

You care about health, fitness, and helping people start — and stick with — better habits. You’re motivated by the craft of turning curiosity into membership and first value.

• You bias to action, then measure. You ship small, learn, and compound.
• You raise concerns early and bring possible solutions when experiments or funnels look wrong.
• You share context, invite feedback, and keep partners aligned on metrics and tradeoffs.
• You take ownership from discovery through production support on the paths you ship.

Notre équipe a développé une méthode qui y répond de façon exacte pour les modèles bayésiens. title: Intern AI Researcher: Anomaly Detection for Predictive Maintenance in Distributed Storage
description:
## About Scality
Scality builds data infrastructure software for enterprise AI, cyber resilience, and sovereign control at multi-petabyte to exabyte scale. Its AI Data Infrastructure platform reduces operational burden through AI-powered autonomous operations while aligning the right storage media, performance, and protection to each workload through human-approved lifecycle policies.
Built on CORE5 cyber resilience and open-code principles, Scality software delivers extreme performance, operational simplicity, and sustainable economics.
The world's most demanding enterprises and government organizations depend on Scality to power AI initiatives, defend critical data, and build infrastructure that lasts for decades. Recognized as a leader by Gartner, Scality is where AI remembers, learns, and thinks. F
Follow us on LinkedIn. Visit www.scality.com and our blog.
Context & Motivation
A distributed storage cluster continuously emits telemetry at every level, from the platform and S3 service down to each server and disk. A failing disk, server or storage node leaves traces in these multivariate time series, from subtle shifts in a few metrics to system-wide disruption. Detecting and diagnosing these anomalies early is critical for:
• Predictive maintenance: isolating or replacing a component before it impacts service
• Faster diagnosis: pointing support engineers to the root cause, not just to an alert
• Higher availability and durability of customer data
This internship is part of a joint research project between Scality and an INRIA research team. The project released SHAD (Scality High-dimensional Anomaly Detection), an open benchmark published at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track). It contains 215 real 171-dimensional time series from Scality RING clusters, annotated for injected disk, server and storage-node failures. SHAD's baselines show the problem is far from solved. No detector handles every failure type, per-dimension attributions find root causes no better than chance, and off-the-shelf LLMs cannot interpret the anomalies. This internship builds on SHAD to close these gaps.
More details on the project: scality.github.io/shad
Your Mission
As part of our R&D team and in close collaboration with INRIA researchers, you will develop AI models that detect, explain and interpret anomalies in storage-cluster telemetry. Your work will include:
1. State of the Art
Review the literature and open-source projects on multivariate time series anomaly detection, root-cause attribution and LLM-based interpretation of time series. Also survey recent work on AI agents that automate research and experimentation. Starting points include SHAD and the TSB-AD benchmark.
2. Anomaly Detection & Diagnosis Models
Design, train and benchmark models that improve on SHAD's baselines at each stage of the pipeline:
• Detection that stays accurate across disk, server and storage-node failures (e.g., ensembles, hybrid models, time series foundation models)
• Explanation: attributing each anomaly to the dimensions that actually cause it
• Interpretation: turning detections into actionable diagnoses (failure type, criticality, affected component)
• Early detection of progressive degradations, the core of predictive maintenance
3. Fleets of AI Agents for Research
Set up and manage fleets of AI agents that run your studies at scale:
• Design agent workflows that launch experiments, run benchmarks and compare methods
• Orchestrate and monitor many agents working in parallel
• Build safeguards for rigor: experiment tracking, reproducibility, independent verification of results
• Assess what agent-driven research changes in practice: speed, coverage, failure modes
4. Evaluation & Validation
Evaluate every model with rigorous, reproducible protocols. Use them to:
• Measure each stage with SHAD's metrics (VUS-PR for detection, NDCG for explanation, a questionnaire for interpretation)
Quantify performance per failure family and scenario
• Identify which approaches are ready to transfer to production monitoring
Expected Outcomes & Valorization
Depending on results, the work may be valorized through:
• A scientific publication with the Scality and INRIA researchers
• New methods and baselines contributed to the open-source SHAD benchmark
• Reusable agent-based research workflows for the R&D team
Technical Stack
• Python (primary language for modeling, experimentation and analysis)
• PyTorch and scikit-learn (deep learning and classical models)
• SHAD benchmark (github.com/scality/shad) and TSB-AD (github.com/TheDatumOrg/TSB-AD) for data, detectors and evaluation
• LLM-based AI agents and their orchestration tooling
Candidate Profile
• Final-year student in a Master's program or Engineering school (Bac+5), in machine learning, data science or computer science
• Solid foundations in machine learning; experience with time series or anomaly detection is a strong plus
• Strong interest in LLMs and AI agents, and curiosity for new ways of doing research
• Good Python skills and hands-on experience with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch
• Rigorous and critical with experimental results, especially when agents produce them
• Autonomous and curious, able to communicate results clearly in written and spoken English
• Interest in distributed systems or storage is a plus, not a prerequisite
Work Environment
You will join a fast-paced, lean AI R&D team. French and English is our primary working language. You will benefit from:
• Mentorship from R&D engineers
• Close collaboration with INRIA researchers working on time series anomaly detection
• Access to real telemetry from Scality RING clusters and to the AI agent tooling the team uses for its studies
• A high-trust environment where your findings will directly influence engineering decisions
Why Join Scality?
• Work on a concrete research problem with real-world industrial impact
• Build on a benchmark published at NeurIPS and contribute to open research
• Practice a new way of doing research, with fleets of AI agents as research assistants
• Be part of a team building infrastructure trusted by Fortune 500 companies
• Potential to publish research or continue as a full-time engineer after the internship

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.
We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

Building and operating large-scale, distributed web crawlers that discover, fetch, and extract data across billions of pages reliably and efficiently.

Creating tooling and infrastructure that lets researchers request, monitor, and explore newly crawled web data quickly and reliably.

Hands-on experience building and scaling web crawlers or scraping systems, ideally in support of machine learning training data.
Strong engineering skills in distributed systems at scale (e.g., Kubernetes, queue-based architectures, or custom pipelines processing billions of documents).
The capacity to autonomously evaluate the quality, coverage, and compliance of crawled data, and to build the tooling to measure it.

At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.
MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour.
We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.
MSF International
Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 26 sections, 28 associations and 16 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.
I. CONTEXT
MSF consists of 6 Operational Centres (OCs) and 3 European Supply Centres (ESCs). In the supply domain there is a joint Supply Tansformational Topics Roadmap composed by several inter-OC and inter-ESC projects, and their number is growing due to the need to increase cooperation between MSF entities while improving the quality of MSF's supply chain. The capacity to measure performance and analyse data across different entities is therefore essential and is contributing to MSF ambitions on interoperability and climate.
The role of the International Office is to foster cooperation and coordination between MSF entities. The Supply Data Analyst will therefore act as a facilitator between the OCs and ESCs: bringing their representatives together, helping them build shared approaches on supply data and performance, and turning these agreements into concrete deliverables.
The Global Supply Data & Analytics (GSDA) team (previously SCPM) has been actively working to build the analytical and data foundations needed to support a global approach to supply chain performance management, and to contribute to the governance of supply data across entities. The team is led by the Supply Chain Analytics Manager and includes one Data Analysts and one data governance specialist; the Supply Data Analyst will join it as an additional analyst.
Reporting hierarchically and functionally to the Supply Chain Analytics Manager, the Supply Data Analyst will: collaborate closely with the supply chain professionals responsible for BI and performance management within the 6 OCs and 3 ESCs; work in close link with the ShARP (Shared Analytics and Reporting Project) team in SITS (Shared IT Services); on the existing UniField intersection reports; work alongside the GSDA team and the IO Supply team on projects related to supply chain data analytics; and interact with stakeholders across MSF, including finance, IT, medical, pharmacy, logistics and operations teams.
II. PURPOSE OF THE JOB
The Supply Data Analyst supports supply chain performance analysis and decision making across MSF by delivering reliable data, KPIs, reports and actionable recommendations. The position also fosters cooperation between the OCs and ESCs around shared supply data, turning agreements into concrete deliverables.
Within GSDA, the Supply Data Analyst will support the growing need for data management, reporting and analytics from the supply chain teams, including the monitoring of KPIs and the analysis of data coming from MSF information systems (such as UniField, Isystock or Akiba).
III. ACCOUNTABILITIES
The Supply Data Analyst is accountable for the following expected results and the activities deployed to achieve them.
1. UniField intersection reports are reliable, relevant and meet the needs of the OCs
a. Take over the existing UniField intersection reports in close link with the ShARP team and improve them (reliability, relevance, usability) based on users' feedback and identified gaps
b. Collect the reporting needs of each OC and consolidate them into a clear, prioritised set of requirements
c. Design and deliver new intersection reports in coordination with the ShARP team, with validation from the OC representatives
2. Supply data is available and of reliable quality for analysis
a. Extract, clean and consolidate supply data from UniField and other information systems
b. Check data consistency and quality, and report anomalies to the relevant teams
c. Document data sources, definitions and calculation methods
3. KPIs and reporting solutions support decision making
a. Calculate and update a set of KPIs on a regular basis, in coordination with the teams concerned
b. Build and maintain ad hoc data reporting solutions (Power BI) providing visuals that accurately summarise supply chain activities while providing actionable insights
c. Support the teams in the definition of additional KPIs as needs arise
4. Stakeholders receive relevant data analysis and actionable recommendations
a. Support stakeholders on supply data analysis
b. Respond to ad hoc data and analysis requests using supply data from different stakeholders (supply, finance, medical…)
c. Present analysis results and recommendations in a clear way to non-technical audiences
5. Cooperation between the OCs and ESCs on supply data produces concrete deliverables
a. Convene and facilitate working groups and meetings with representatives of each OC and ESC, from preparation (agenda, pre-alignment of positions) to follow-up (minutes, actions, deadlines)
b. Lead discussions between entities with different needs and practices, and build compromises and consensus on shared definitions, KPIs and ways of working
c. Turn agreements into concrete deliverables (e.g., shared KPI definitions, dashboards, documentation) and follow their delivery
6. Data-related tools and processes improve continuously and stakeholders are kept informed
a. Contribute to the improvement of data-related tools and processes within the team
b. Proactively identify data needs, risks and improvement opportunities, and propose solutions autonomously
c. Manage stakeholders and expectations: identify their needs, keep them informed, and escalate blockers to the Supply Chain Analytics Manager when needed
IV. AUTONOMY, COMPLEXITY
Challenges and decisions that the job faces to achieve the accountabilities:
Autonomy to think and act: works with limited supervision; takes initiative, prioritises and drives work to completion, proactively identifies data needs, risks and improvement opportunities, and escalates blockers to the Supply Chain Analytics Manager when needed.
Complexity of the environment: works across 6 OCs and 3 ESCs with different needs, practices and information systems (UniField, Isystock, Akiba); builds compromises on shared definitions and KPIs, handles multiple priorities at once, and interacts with technical and non-technical stakeholders (finance, IT, medical, pharmacy, logistics, operations) in a cross-cultural and cross-functional environment.
SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE
The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others.
Education
Bachelor's level or above in data analytics, statistics, business management, supply chain or a related field, or a combination of relevant education and professional experience (essential)
Experience
Minimum of 2 years of experience as Data Analyst (essential)
Direct work experience involving significant data management (essential)
Experience in facilitating meetings or working groups involving multiple stakeholders and in delivering concrete outputs from them (essential)
Supply chain, logistics and Finance experience in NGO's operational settings (desirable)
Previous work experience with UniField, MSF's main ERP software (desirable)
Skills
Strong stakeholder management and facilitation skills: ability to bring together representatives of different entities, lead effective meetings, negotiate compromises and deliver concrete outcomes
Strong analytical skills
Good organisational skills, ability to handle multiple priorities at one time
Autonomous and proactive: ability to take initiative, prioritise and drive work to completion with limited supervision
Good level skills in Excel, Power BI and database management
Ability to work in a cross-cultural and cross-functional environment
